subject: POC trial planning & workload intake — AcmeHealth
messages:
From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>
To: Alicia Gomez <agomez@acmehealth.com>, Rajesh Singh <rsingh@acmehealth.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, Dylan Brooks <dylan.brooks@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 13 Sep 2027 15:02:00 -0700
Subject: POC trial planning & workload intake — AcmeHealth

Thanks again for the call today — great conversation. Quick recap and next steps to get the POC scoped so we can lock dates.

Scope (as discussed):
- 2-week functional POC followed by a 4-week evaluation window (we'll call this the "trial")
- Primary flows: clinical notes summarization and triage routing (API integration, no PHI storage besides transit)
- Success criteria: accuracy on summary QA set, p95 latency SLA, and cost per 1k tokens — see attached draft success_criteria doc (acme_poc_success_criteria.docx).

What we need from you to finalize plan:
1) Success criteria: any additional KPIs you want tracked besides accuracy/latency/cost?
2) Workload profile: typical RPS, expected token lengths (prompt & response), concurrency, burst patterns (hourly/daily peaks).
3) Ownership: who on your side owns the API integration and who owns clinical QA?

Proposed owners on our side:
- Sales/eng lead: Ben Carter (me) — POC coordination and commercial items
- Workload tuning / observability: Marissa Cole (marissa.cole@redwood.ai)
- Infra / test harness / deployment: Dylan Brooks (dylan.brooks@redwood.ai)

Proposed timeline:
- Kickoff call: week of Sep 20 (please confirm availability)
- POC prep & infra: Sep 21–30
- Trial start: Oct 1
- Checkpoints: weekly (Oct 8, Oct 15) and final evaluation Oct 15–Oct 31

I've attached a draft success criteria doc and a CSV template for traffic profiles — fill in and send back when convenient. Happy to take a quick workshop to fill the traffic profile with you.

Thanks,
Ben
Ben Carter | Solutions Director
Redwood Inference
ben.carter@redwood.ai | +1 (415) 555-0123

Attachments: acme_poc_success_criteria.docx (draft), acme_traffic_profile.csv (template)

From: Alicia Gomez <agomez@acmehealth.com>
To: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, Dylan Brooks <dylan.brooks@redwood.ai>
Cc: Rajesh Singh <rsingh@acmehealth.com>
Date: Tue, 14 Sep 2027 09:18:00 -0700
Subject: Re: POC trial planning & workload intake — AcmeHealth

Thanks Ben — appreciate the clear recap. We're aligned on the scope. Answers below and I've attached our traffic export for the last 30 days (acme_traffic_profile.csv).

Success criteria (priority order):
- Summary accuracy: >= 85% F1 on our labeled QA set (we'll share a 200-item set)
- Latency: p95 < 500ms for single-shot summarization requests (end-to-end)
- Cost: target <$0.30 per 1k tokens in production; for trial we care more about quality than absolute cost
- Reliability: <1% error rate for API responses during business hours

Workload profile (from attached):
- Sustained RPS (typical): 5 req/s
- Concurrency: 6 active concurrent callers during business hours; peak concurrency seen: 18
- Burst patterns: hourly micro-bursts up to 50 req/s for ~1–2 minutes (e.g., batch ingest after clinic hours), daily ramp at 09:00–11:00 and 14:00–15:00
- Tokens: average prompt length 80 tokens, average response length 150 tokens; 95th percentile prompt 420 tokens when long clinical notes are included
- Request types: 70% single-shot summarization, 20% multi-turn clarification (short), 10% reranking/metadata extraction

Other notes/questions:
- Data residency: Must remain in US region; do you support region pinning for the trial?
- Logging/audit: We need access to request/response logs for QA but cannot store transcripts beyond 30 days; can Redwood provide log streaming to our S3?

Ownership on our side:
- API integration lead: Alicia Gomez (me)
- Clinical QA: Rajesh Singh (cc'd)

Happy to confirm kickoff next week — we are fairly open Wed/Thu morning PT.

Thanks,
Alicia
Alicia Gomez | Senior Product Manager
AcmeHealth
agomez@acmehealth.com | (650) 555-0199

Attachment: acme_traffic_profile.csv

From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>
To: Alicia Gomez <agomez@acmehealth.com>, Rajesh Singh <rsingh@acmehealth.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, Dylan Brooks <dylan.brooks@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 14 Sep 2027 13:40:00 -0700
Subject: Re: POC trial planning & workload intake — AcmeHealth

Alicia — perfect, this is exactly what we need. Quick responses to your questions and proposed next steps.

1) Region pinning & logs: Yes, we can pin the trial to our US region and set up a log stream to your S3 with 30-day retention. Marissa will own the log config and the S3 integration.

2) Measuring success: We'll run "shadow" runs against a copy of your QA set and measure F1/recall/precision, plus synthetic traffic to validate p95 latency under your reported burst profile. For cost, we'll provide a trial cost projection based on the traffic profile you sent.

3) Test harness & infra: Dylan will provision the test harness, set up metrics (latency, error rates, tokens), and run the synthetic bursts (we'll coordinate timing).

4) Owners & timeline (updated):
- Kickoff workshop (tech + QA): Wed, Sep 22 at 09:30 PT — proposed (please confirm)
- Prep window: Sep 23–30 (integration test + baseline runs)
- Trial start: Oct 1 (2 weeks active trial + 2-week observation window)

5) Checkpoints & deliverables:
- Week 1 (Oct 8): baseline accuracy & latency report; initial tuning recommendations
- Week 2 (Oct 15): tuned config + updated accuracy/cost projections
- Final evaluation: Oct 22–Oct 31 (final report & recommended production config)

Marissa and Dylan, please confirm you can take ownership of the items above. Alicia/Rajesh — if that kickoff time works, I will send a calendar invite and a short agenda (30–45m).

Best,
Ben
